title: Produce functional and non-functional requirements files
goal: Produce reviewable functional and non-functional requirements documents from the initial project information and completed interview before feature and MVP scope selection.
in_scope: Update the project-local requirements-interview skill to create separate Markdown files for functional and non-functional requirements as outputs of requirements discovery.
Add concise blank functional and non-functional requirements templates to the skill's assets and direct the skill to copy and adapt them for each project.
Use requirements/functional-requirements.md and requirements/non-functional-requirements.md by default, adapting to existing project documentation conventions when present.

Give each requirement a stable identifier and distinguish confirmed requirements, assumptions, and unresolved questions; preserve traceability to user-provided information or interview decisions where practical.
For functional requirements, capture relevant actor or context, expected behavior, applicable conditions or exceptions, and acceptance or verification notes where known.
For non-functional requirements, capture relevant quality or constraint expectations and measurable targets when known; do not invent thresholds or force irrelevant categories.
Present both files to the user for review and corrections before mapping implementation features or selecting the MVP scope.
Keep MVP.md as a concise summary and link or point to the two requirements files.
out_of_scope: Implementing product features described by the requirements.
Generating requirements from unsupported assumptions or fabricating measurable targets.
acceptance_criteria: The skill specifies separate, discoverable functional and non-functional requirements files with stable requirement IDs.
The skill contains reusable functional and non-functional requirements templates with clear placeholders and no example requirement that could be mistaken for a confirmed decision.
The files distinguish confirmed content from assumptions and unresolved questions and retain source traceability where practical.
Functional requirements capture behavior and applicable exceptions; non-functional requirements capture relevant quality expectations and targets only when supported by interview information.
Both documents are reviewed and corrected by the user before feature mapping and MVP scope selection begin.
MVP.md remains a concise summary that points to the requirements documents.
The skill does not invent requirement thresholds or force non-applicable quality categories.
